claim: The TZ at the mouse Tfap2c-Bmp7 locus consists of seven CTCF-binding sites: L1, L2, L3, L4, R1, R2, and R3.
source: The TZ consists of seven binding sites of CTCF: they are L1, L2, L3, L4, R1, R2, and R3, arrayed in this order from the Tfap2c side to the Bmp7 side (Figure 1A; Tsujimura et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and references a previous publication (Tsujimura et al., 2018) as well as Figure 1A.

claim: L1-L4 CTCF-binding sites are oriented towards Tfap2c and R1-R3 are oriented towards Bmp7.
source: L1-L4 are oriented towards Tfap2c and collectively referred to as L, while R1-R3 are towards Bmp7 and referred to as R.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Native ChIP failed to detect CTCF binding at L1 and L4, suggesting weak or indirect binding.
source: However, native-ChIP (nChIP) failed to detect CTCF binding at L1 and L4, suggesting the binding there is weak or indirect (Tsujimura et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: STITCH is a synthetic DNA cassette consisting of 178 or 179 bp DNA sequences carrying CTCF-binding motifs concatenated together.
source: We extracted the 178 or 179 bp DNA sequences carrying the motif sequences for CTCF binding and concatenated them as a short DNA cassette.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text describing the design of STITCH.

claim: STITCH contains tetO sequences embedded at four different positions within the cassette.
source: We embedded the core sequence of the tetracycline operator (tetO) at four different positions within the cassette.
evidence: The claim is explicitly stated in the text describing STITCH design.

claim: tetO is bound by tetR in the absence of doxycycline, allowing recruitment of a linked effector protein.
source: tetO is bound by the tetracycline repressor (tetR), but not in the presence of doxycycline (DOX), and thus allows recruitment of a linked effector protein to the cassette in a drug-dependent manner (Gossen and Bujard, 1992).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation to Gossen and Bujard, 1992.

claim: STITCH includes a puromycin-resistant gene sandwiched by two loxP sites for efficient targeting.
source: We also put a puromycin-resistant gene (PUROr) sandwiched by two loxP sites for the sake of efficient targeting (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: MYC is highly expressed in human pluripotent stem cells.
source: MYC is highly expressed in human pluripotent stem cells (Knoepfler, 2008).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: MYC expression is regulated by long-range enhancers in various cell types.
source: As MYC expression is regulated by long-range enhancers in various cell types, we thought that MYC expression in the stem cells should also be dependent on long-range enhancers (Bahr et al., 2018; Cho et al., 2018; Dave et al., 2017; Herranz et al., 2014; Hnisz et al., 2013; Lovén et al., 2013; Pulikkan et al., 2018; Shi et al., 2013; Sur et al., 2012; Uslu et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by multiple citations.

claim: A large contact domain around MYC in human embryonic stem cells spans almost 3 Mb.
source: A previous study called a large contact domain around MYC in human embryonic stem cells (ESCs) spanning almost 3 Mb (Dixon et al., 2015; Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a citation, and referenced in Figure 1B.

claim: A super-enhancer region is annotated within the PVT1 gene in ESCs based on H3K27ac ChIP-seq and ChIP-STARR-seq.
source: A super-enhancer region is annotated within the neighboring long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) gene PVT1 in ESCs based on ChIP-seq for histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), the enhancer associated histone modification, and ChIP-STARR-seq (self-transcribing active regulatory region sequencing, after chromatin immunoprecipitation) (Barakat et al., 2018; Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a citation, and referenced in Figure 1B.

claim: A super-enhancer was annotated within the same region in mouse ESCs.
source: Similarly, a super-enhancer was annotated within the same region in the mouse ESCs (Witte et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Broad deposition of H3K27ac is present around the PVT1 region in the human iPSC line.
source: We also confirmed the broad deposition of H3K27ac around there in the human iPSC line (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and referenced in Figure 1B showing experimental data.

claim: A 3 Mb region around MYC was deleted from one allele to make the locus locally haploid.
source: Since the diploidy would hamper the following genome editing procedures, we first deleted one allele of the 3 Mb region around MYC as described before (Tsujimura et al., 2018) to make the locus locally haploid, and termed the clone as 'Hap' (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a citation, and referenced in Figure 1B.

claim: STITCH was inserted into five different positions of the MYC locus: STITCH+30kb, STITCH+440kb, STITCH+1760kb, STITCH+1790kb, and STITCH-30kb.
source: Then we inserted STITCH into five different positions of the remaining allele of the locus: 'STITCH+30kb', 'STITCH+440kb', 'STITCH+1760kb' and 'STITCH+1790kb' have the STITCH insertions away from the MYC promoter for the indicated distances to the telomeric side of the q arm of the chromosome (the right side on the map, Figure 1B); 'STITCH-30kb', at the 30 kb upstream from MYC (the left side, Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and referenced in Figure 1B.

claim: In the wild type allele of Hap, MYC mainly contacts with the PVT1 region.
source: In the wild type allele of Hap, MYC mainly contacts with the PVT1 region and around (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: In STITCH+30kb, STITCH+440kb, and STITCH-30kb, the contacts were blocked at the inserted positions of STITCH.
source: In STITCH+30kb, STITCH+440kb, and STITCH-30kb, the contacts were blocked at the inserted positions of STITCH as expected (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Only STITCH+30kb strongly down-regulated MYC expression, while the other insertions did not.
source: We found that only STITCH+30kb strongly down-regulated the MYC expression, while the others did not (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The region between STITCH+30kb and STITCH+440kb (+(30-440)kb region) possesses the enhancer for MYC expression.
source: These results suggest that the region between STITCH+30kb and STITCH+440kb (+(30-440)kb region) possesses the enhancer for the MYC expression.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: Deletion of the +(30-440)kb region strongly down-regulated MYC expression.
source: While the 4C contact profile of MYC extended further away from the deleted region (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), MYC was strongly down-regulated by the deletion (Figure 1D), showing that the region contains the responsible enhancer.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Each of the CTCF-binding sites of STITCH, except L1 and L4, was bound by CTCF in human iPSCs.
source: nChIP-seq in STITCH+30kb confirmed that each of the binding sites of STITCH, except L1 and L4, was bound by CTCF as in the endogenous mouse genome, showing that these CTCF bindings are recapitulated regardless of the genomic context in human iPSCs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: STITCH recruits CTCF and blocks the gene-enhancer interaction when located in between as an insulator.
source: Thus, STITCH recruits CTCF and blocks the gene-enhancer interaction when located in between as an insulator.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: MYC carries two CTCF-binding sites directed to the right side near the promoter region.
source: As indicated, MYC carries two CTCF-binding sites directed to the right side near the promoter region.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on nChIP-seq data.

claim: These CTCF-binding sites near MYC may account for the directional bias of MYC contact towards the right side in WT(Hap).
source: These sites may account for the directional bias of the MYC contact towards the right side in WT(Hap) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Deletion and duplication of the whole PVT1 genic region, as well as RNAi knockdown, has suggested a role for the PVT1 lncRNA in MYC activation.
source: Of note, deletion and duplication of the whole PVT1 genic region, as well as the knockdown experiment via RNAi, has suggested a role for the PVT1 lncRNA in MYC activation (Tseng et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: A recent study shows that inhibition of PVT1 transcription does not impact MYC expression in a cancer cell line.
source: Indeed, a recent study shows that inhibition of the PVT1 transcription does not impact on MYC expression in a cancer cell line (Cho et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The PVT1 promoter modulates MYC expression as a competitor for enhancer activity.
source: This study instead showed that the PVT1 promoter modulates MYC expression as a competitor for enhancer activity, which may indicate that the transcribed RNA is a byproduct.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a finding from a cited study.

claim: Strong down-regulation of MYC was confirmed in both STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) by RNA-seq.
source: Consistently with the qPCR assay (Figure 1D), strong down-regulation of MYC was confirmed in both STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: PVT1 expression was not altered in STITCH+30kb.
source: PVT1 expression was not altered in STITCH+30kb (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: No other detectable expression changes around the MYC locus were observed in either STITCH+30kb or del(30-440).
source: We did not observe other detectable expression changes around the MYC locus in either STITCH+30kb or del(30-440) (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Down-regulated genes in both STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) are highly enriched with known MYC target genes.
source: Strikingly, the down-regulated genes in both STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) are highly enriched with known MYC target genes, showing that the down-regulation of MYC by both mutations is large enough to affect its target transcriptome.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on GSEA analysis.

claim: The enriched categories in GSEA are well shared by STITCH+30kb and del(30-440), highlighting the similarity in transcriptomic change.
source: The other enriched categories are also well shared by the two mutations, highlighting the similarity in the transcriptomic change.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on GSEA analysis.

claim: STITCH+30kb had 218 down-regulated genes and 494 up-regulated genes with log2 fold change >0.5 and p-adjusted <0.05.
source: With threshold of log2 fold change <0.5 and p-adjusted <0.05, STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) had 218 and 68 down-regulated genes, and 494 and 137 up-regulated genes, respectively (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: del(30-440) had 68 down-regulated genes and 137 up-regulated genes with log2 fold change >0.5 and p-adjusted <0.05.
source: With threshold of log2 fold change <0.5 and p-adjusted <0.05, STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) had 218 and 68 down-regulated genes, and 494 and 137 up-regulated genes, respectively (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Large fractions of differentially expressed genes (36 down-regulated and 92 up-regulated) were common between STITCH+30kb and del(30-440).
source: Among those, large fractions (36 and 92 genes, for down- and up-regulation, respectively) were common between the two alleles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The comparison between STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) called much less number (64) of differentially expressed genes.
source: Importantly, the comparison between STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) called much less number (64) of differentially expressed genes (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: del(30-440) exhibited a rather milder effect on the transcriptome than STITCH+30kb.
source: Moreover, del(30-440) exhibited a rather milder effect on the transcriptome than STITCH+30kb (Figure 2B and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: PVT1 has little impact on the transcriptome as trans-acting lncRNA.
source: These data suggest that PVT1 has little impact on the transcriptome as trans-acting lncRNA if any.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: The insulation showed a stronger effect than the deletion of the enhancer.
source: It should be noted that the insulation showed a stronger effect than the deletion of the enhancer.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on comparison of experimental results.

claim: STITCH+440kb did not show almost any effect on the MYC expression level.
source: STITCH+440kb did not show almost any effect on the MYC expression level (Figure 1C,D), indicating that the region beyond +440 kb does not contribute to the activation of MYC when the locus is intact.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Upon deletion of the enhancer, contacts of MYC greatly extended beyond +440 kb.
source: However, upon the deletion of the enhancer, contacts of MYC greatly extended beyond +440 kb (Figure 1C,E, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: MYC can be slightly activated by regions with some enhancer activity located beyond +440 kb that do not associate with MYC in the normal context.
source: Therefore it might be possible that MYC can be slightly activated by regions with some enhancer activity located beyond +440 kb that do not associate with MYC in the normal context, which may account for the milder outcome of del(30-440) than STITCH+30kb.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a speculative explanation for the observed data.

claim: The categories enriched in down-regulated genes include those in which MYC has been implicated by previous studies such as cell cycle progression, unfolded protein response, TCA cycle, mTORC1 signaling, and cholesterol synthesis.
source: The categories enriched in down-regulated genes include those in which MYC has been implicated by previous studies such as cell cycle progression (Bretones et al., 2015), unfolded protein response (Shajahan-Haq et al., 2014), TCA cycle (Anderson et al., 2018), mTORC1 signaling (Liu et al., 2017; Yue et al., 2017), and cholesterol synthesis (Hofmann et al., 2015; Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by multiple citations, and referenced in Figure 2E.

claim: Commonly down-regulated genes in STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) are highly enriched with genes encoding regulators of ribosome assembly.
source: Also, gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis shows that the commonly down-regulated genes in STITCH+30kb and del(30-440) are highly enriched with genes encoding regulators of ribosome assembly, which are known target groups of MYC in various systems (Hofmann et al., 2015; Uslu et al., 2014; van Riggelen et al., 2010; Zeller et al., 2006), as well as those involved in cholesterol metabolism similarly as above (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by multiple citations, and referenced in a figure.

claim: Deletion and inversion of either of the two CTCF binding arrays, L or R, impaired, but still kept, the blocking activity of the TZ at the endogenous locus in mouse ESCs.
source: In fact, deletion and inversion of either of the two CTCF binding arrays, L or R, impaired, but still kept, the blocking activity of the TZ at the endogenous locus in the mouse ESCs (Tsujimura et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The MYC expression levels in delL and delR were slightly increased from the original STITCH allele.
source: The MYC expression levels in delL and delR were slightly increased from the original STITCH allele (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: invR also increased MYC expression but to a lesser extent than delL and delR.
source: invR also increased it but to a lesser extent (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: del(L2-R2) and del(L1-R2) up-regulated MYC expression even more, but much less than the wild type Hap allele.
source: del(L2-R2) and del(L1-R2) up-regulated the expression even more, but much less than the wild type Hap allele (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The MYC expression in del(L1-R3) was comparable to that of Hap, showing that gene activation could be safely recovered upon removal of the CTCF-binding sites.
source: The MYC expression in del(L1-R3) was comparable to that of Hap, showing that the gene activation could be safely recovered upon removal of the CTCF-binding sites (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: inv(L1-R3) exhibited the same degree of repression as STITCH+30kb, showing that STITCH blocks enhancer activation regardless of the orientation of the insertion as a whole.
source: inv(L1-R3) exhibited the same degree of repression as STITCH+30kb, showing that STITCH blocks enhancer activation regardless of the orientation of the insertion as a whole (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The contact frequency with the +(30-440)kb enhancer region was changed depending on the configuration of CTCF-binding sites.
source: The contact frequency with the +(30-440)kb enhancer region was changed depending on the configuration (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The original STITCH and inv(L1-R3) most strongly reduced the contacts with the enhancer region.
source: The original STITCH and inv(L1-R3) most strongly reduced the contacts.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on 4C-seq data.

claim: invR showed slightly more contacts with the enhancer region than the original STITCH, but not as much as delL and delR.
source: invR showed slightly more of contacts there, but not as much as delL and delR.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on 4C-seq data.

claim: The divergent configuration is the strongest way to block contacts.
source: These results indicate firstly that the divergent configuration is the strongest way to block contacts, and secondly that the more CTCF binds there, the more strongly it blocks contacts (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results shown in figures.

claim: The more CTCF binds at STITCH, the more strongly it blocks contacts.
source: These results indicate firstly that the divergent configuration is the strongest way to block contacts, and secondly that the more CTCF binds there, the more strongly it blocks contacts (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results shown in figures.

claim: The gene expression level and the contact frequency are well correlated.
source: Thus, the gene expression level and the contact frequency are well correlated.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on comparison of gene expression and 4C-seq data.

claim: The Spearman's rank correlation coefficients between gene expression and contact frequency were 0.92 and 0.90 for VP-MYC1 and VP-MYC2, respectively.
source: The Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were 0.92 and 0.90 for VP-MYC1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B) and VP-MYC2 (Figure 3I), respectively.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The expression level fits with a power-law model with the contact frequency of the +(30-440)kb region with a scaling exponent of 4.1–4.3.
source: We noted that the expression level fits with a power-law model with the contact frequency of the +(30-440)kb region with a scaling exponent of 4.1–4.3 (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Even del(L1-R2) efficiently blocks gene activation only with the remaining one CTCF-binding site R3, but not much the contact.
source: It is particularly notable that even the del(L1-R2) efficiently blocks the gene activation only with the remaining one CTCF-binding site R3, but not much the contact.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an observation from the experimental results.

claim: The Hap allele without the STITCH insertion exhibits overall rightward directionality of chromatin folding from VP-MYC1/2 till VP-STITCH-left/right.
source: The Hap allele without the STITCH insertion exhibits overall rightward directionality from VP-MYC1/2 till VP-STITCH-left/right (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The insertion of STITCH introduced a skewed change of the directionality across the insertion site.
source: The insertion of STITCH introduced a skewed change of the directionality across the insertion site.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text based on 4C-seq data analysis.

claim: The rightward directionality at VP-STITCH-right was enhanced by STITCH insertion, while those at VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left were decreased to neutral.
source: The rightward directionality at VP-STITCH-right was even more enhanced, while those at VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left were decreased to neutral (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: In delR, the directionality at VP-STITCH-right became less prominent than the intact STITCH allele.
source: In delR, the directionality at VP-STITCH-right became less prominent than the intact STITCH allele, while the directionality at both VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left was again neutral (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: In delL, the rightward directionality was kept or slightly enhanced at both VP-STITCH-left and -right, while the directionality at VP-MYC1/2 was marginally reduced from the wild type allele.
source: By contrast, in delL, the rightward directionality was kept or slightly enhanced at both VP-STITCH-left and -right, while the directionality at VP-MYC1/2 was marginally reduced from the wild type allele (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The array L mainly orients the folding directionality at VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left relatively towards the left side.
source: These results suggest that the array L mainly orients the folding directionality at VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left relatively towards the left side, while the array R enhances the rightward directionality at VP-STITCH-right.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: The array R enhances the rightward directionality at VP-STITCH-right.
source: These results suggest that the array L mainly orients the folding directionality at VP-MYC1/2 and VP-STITCH-left relatively towards the left side, while the array R enhances the rightward directionality at VP-STITCH-right.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: Neither the diverging configuration of CTCF-binding sites nor the diverging directionality of chromatin folding is a prerequisite for enhancer blocking.
source: These results suggest that neither the diverging configuration of CTCF-binding sites nor the diverging directionality of chromatin folding is a prerequisite for enhancer blocking.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: The PCA plot segregated the non-blocking alleles from the blocking ones along the PC1 axis.
source: The PCA plot well segregated the non-blocking alleles (Hap and del(L1-R3)) from the other blocking ones, especially the original STITCH, inv(L1-R3) along the PC1 axis (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The segregation in PCA is mostly explained by lower and higher contact frequencies in the left side region, and higher and lower frequencies in the 570 kb region from the +30 kb site to the right side, of the non-blocking and the blocking alleles, respectively.
source: The component loadings of PC1 show that the segregation is mostly explained by lower and higher contact frequencies in the left side region, and higher and lower frequencies in the 570 kb region from the +30 kb site to the right side, of the non-blocking and the blocking alleles, respectively (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: MYC has preferential contacts with the super-enhancer/PVT1 region more than with the other non-active regions in the absence of CTCF insulation.
source: These results suggest that MYC has preferential contacts with the super-enhancer/PVT1 region more than with the other non-active regions in the absence of the CTCF insulation.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from PCA analysis.

claim: The power-law scaling of MYC expression with the contact frequency with the PVT1 region has a scaling exponent of 3.6–3.7.
source: We found that the power-law scaling of the MYC expression with the contact frequency with the PVT1 region has a scaling exponent of 3.6–3.7, which is slightly less than with the +(30-440)kb region (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The contact with PVT1 scales with that with the +(30-440)kb region, with an exponent factor 1.14–1.15.
source: Consistently, the contact with PVT1 scales with that with the +(30-440)kb region, with an exponent factor 1.14–1.15, which is slightly higher than the linear correlation (Figure 3J, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: Titration of STITCH insulation revealed that the contact of MYC with the super-enhancer/PVT1 region is enhanced more than the other non-active regions when the insulation is absent.
source: Thus, titration of STITCH insulation revealed that the contact of MYC with the super-enhancer/PVT1 region is enhanced more than the other non-active regions when the insulation is absent.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: The presence of CTCF insulation effectively impairs the gene-enhancer contact more than the contacts with neutral regions.
source: In other words, the presence of CTCF insulation effectively impairs the gene-enhancer contact more than the contacts with neutral regions.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: In the wild type allele, MYC is exclusively marked by H3K4me3, but not by H3K27me3.
source: In the wild type allele, MYC is exclusively marked by H3K4me3, but not by H3K27me3.

claim: Upon STITCH insulation, the H3K4me3 deposition at MYC remained, but was markedly decreased.
source: Upon the STITCH insulation, the H3K4me3 deposition remained, but was markedly decreased.

claim: Upon STITCH insulation, H3K27me3 was enriched at MYC.
source: Instead, H3K27me3 was enriched.

claim: The neighboring PVT1 gene was strongly marked by H3K4me3 at the promoter in both wild type and STITCH+30kb conditions.
source: By contrast, the neighboring PVT1 gene was strongly marked by H3K4me3 at the promoter in both conditions (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).

claim: Some typically active (ACTB, NANOG, DPPA4) and repressed (T, HOXD13) genes were constantly marked by either H3K4me3 or H3K27me3, respectively.
source: Some typically active (ACTB, NANOG, DPPA4) and repressed (T, HOXD13) genes were constantly marked by either H3K4me3 or H3K27me3, respectively (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.

claim: The H3K27ac mark around the super-enhancer region was similarly observed in both wild type and STITCH+30kb alleles.
source: Also, the H3K27ac mark around the super-enhancer region was similarly observed in both alleles (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,B).

claim: The peaks at MYC were ranked as one of the top peaks exhibiting the largest fold change for both H3K4me3 and H3K27me3.
source: Among the peaks that were called in at least two out of the total four experiments (two from Hap and the other two from STITCH+30kb), the peaks at MYC were ranked as one of the top peaks exhibiting the largest fold change for both H3K4me3 (Figure 4C) and H3K27me3 (Figure 4D), while the H3K27ac peaks around PVT1 did not change much (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by data shown in figures.
